business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Remarketing of Secondhand Hydraulic Earthmovers and Rollers

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Quebec private law follows the civilian tradition (Civil Code of Quebec), while federal public, criminal, and tax law applies common-law doctrine; corporate law is statutory under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force July 1, 2020
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union, provisionally applied since September 21, 2017
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada December 30, 2018
Canada-United States Convention with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (1980), as amended by the 1984, 1995, 1997 and 2007 Protocols
Canada Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (FIPAs) network, including treaties in force with Panama, Ukraine, Uruguay, and other states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 140-146 (Register of Individuals with Significant Control, as amended by S.C. 2023, c. 26); Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, s. 462.31; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky), S.C. 2017, c. 21; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2. Quebec: Loi sur les societes par actions (Quebec Business Corporations Act, QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1; Loi sur la publicite legale des entreprises (Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises), CQLR c P-44.1, and its implementing fee schedule, including beneficial-control disclosure requirements; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - Full beneficial-ownership data maintained under the QBCA register of persons having control and the federal RISC register is accessible only to authorized government bodies (FINTRAC, CRA, RCMP, CSIS, and provincial analogues), while the REQ public registry discloses director names and addresses; a 25% ownership or voting threshold triggers mandatory beneficial-control declaration.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the home-country competent authority; where the home state is not a Hague Apostille Convention member, Consular Legalization by the competent Canadian diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Corporate Status for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation (for Canada: Corporations Canada or Registraire des entreprises du Quebec)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the originating state is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board resolution authorizing incorporation in Quebec and appointing the local registered office agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notarizing public officer of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the home-country competent authority; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Certificate of Corporate Existence for each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction company registry or authorized registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the home-country competent authority; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and source-of-funds letter covering the settling entity and beneficial owners (required for enhanced-risk cross-border machinery trade)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the UBO's or settling entity's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where available; otherwise notarized bank letter accepted by the Quebec filing agent for KYC purposes

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against the UN Consolidated List (implemented under the United Nations Act), the Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List issued under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Act), the OFAC SDN List as a prudent banking counterparty check, and domestic PEP lists covering senior federal and Quebec public-office holders. FINTRAC's PCMLTFA regime requires identification, verification, and enhanced monitoring of foreign PEPs, with risk-based measures for domestic PEPs in line with FATF Recommendation 12; the medium-risk enhanced classification for used heavy machinery cross-border trading triggers mandatory source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation for wire transfers and SWIFT documentary credits.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - online name reservation and enterprise registration portal at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; federal alternative: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre at https://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/cc-cc.nsf/eng/home
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), a Quebec corporation's name must be in French or accompanied by a French version; a name in a language other than French is accepted only with exceptional authorization of the Registrar or where a French equivalent is registered simultaneously; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet; permitted legal elements include 'Inc.', 'Corp.', and 'Ltee', and the name must be distinctive and not confusingly similar to an active registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Trust / Fiducie (requires prior authorization of the Autorite des marches financiers)
Royal / Crown / Reine / Roi (implies state patronage)
Canada / Quebec (when used in a manner implying official sponsorship or conflicting with the public register)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The REQ name reservation holds the cleared name for 90 days and is non-extendable; re-filing is permitted upon lapse. If the Registrar rejects a name, the promoter receives a refusal notice stating the conflicting register entry or the prohibited token engaged. Within 30 days of refusal, the promoter may file a written demand for administrative review (revision) with the Direction de la publicite legale of the REQ, attaching a comparative table addressing the grounds of distinctive character, typographic or phonetic difference, and absence of confusion. If the review is denied, judicial review may be sought before the Cour du Quebec within 30 days of the reconsideration decision. Concurrently, an alternative name may be reserved de novo to avoid transactional delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible subject to substance conditions: the registered office must be a physical Quebec street address, such as the office of a Quebec notary, lawyer, or licensed domiciliation agent, at which legal process may be served and statutory records inspected; post-office-box-only addresses, virtual mail drops without service capacity, and sham addresses are not accepted; a domiciliation agreement and an REQ head-office declaration are required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate likelihood for an enhanced-risk cross-border trading entity - approximately 25-35% cumulative probability of a registry, tax, or AML compliance inspection within the first 36 months of operation. FINTRAC examinations are generally announced in writing; Revenu Quebec and the CRA may conduct unannounced visits in the course of GST/HST audits, corporate status verifications, and examination of books and records under the Tax Administration Act.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille / consular legalization of the foreign UBO KYC bundle (passport copies, certificate of good standing, board resolution, incumbency certificates)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec (OTTIAQ)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal professional fees for drafting articles of incorporation, by-laws, UBO register, corporate resolutions, and AML onboarding policy

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1 — articles of incorporation (ss. 10-13), first board powers, registered office and corporate records (ss. 24, 29, 35); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44 (ss. 6, 19) as the federal alternative. For this used-construction-excavator reseller with non-resident ownership, the QBCA is the operative statute because Quebec registration, the NEQ and Revenu Québec accounts all attach to the same provincial entity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Direction des entreprises, online portal registrairedesentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation under QBCA Form S-31.1, followed by the Certificate of Incorporation and the initial enterprise registration (NEQ) issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None prescribed by the QBCA: the articles may set zero authorized or paid-in capital, and no escrow account rule applies. If shares are issued at par, at least that par value must be paid in money or property before the share certificate is delivered. A reasonable paid-up capital of CAD 1,000 in cash is recommended to evidence balance-sheet solvency for opening bank facilities, with the remaining funding treated as shareholder loans.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers to the Articles of Incorporation of [CORPORATION NAME] Inc. are confirmed as first directors, holding office until the first annual shareholders' meeting. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the Articles in the Province of Quebec, and the Registraire des entreprises is named filing authority. FURTHER RESOLVED, that President, Secretary and Treasurer are appointed, each authorized to open bank accounts, issue shares, and procure business, environmental and physical permits for used-excavator resale. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the subscription ledger share subscriptions and capital contributions are accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Quebec Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a jurisdiction-wide NUANS search report covering Quebec and reserve the proposed corporate name, e.g. [CORPORATION NAME] Excavator Remarketing Inc., for up to 120 days. Verify that the name is distinctive and does not conflict with any protected name or trademark registered in Quebec. The reservation certificate is then attached to the articles of incorporation in the next step.
required_dossiers: Completed online name-reservation request
NUANS search report (fee paid)
Name-reservation certificate issued by REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusion, file a new name application bearing a coined distinctive element or obtain a written consent letter from the existing nameholder within 30 days, then submit the revised name certificate together with the articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation under the QBCA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — electronic filing chamber
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Articles of Incorporation, list the initial directors, fix the registered office at the Quebec warehouse premises, and define the authorized share structure (common shares without par value). Online electronic signature by each incorporator is accepted; notarization is not mandatory. Pay the CAD 350 incorporation fee and receive the Certificate of Incorporation and the unique enterprise number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (QBCA Form S-31.1)
List of directors with consent signatures
NUANS name-reservation certificate
Electronic authorization of each incorporator
Payment of incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a query regarding signature capacity or missing share rights, file a Notice of Correction with the executed corrected documentation within the 90-day suspension period; alternatively withdraw and refile with a new fee before the certificate is refused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Meeting and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors — internal corporate act at the Quebec registered office; no governmental filing beyond the statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt a unanimous written resolution under QBCA sections 24 and 35. Approve the registered office address, the share subscription table, the banking resolution, and the appointment of President, Secretary and Treasurer. Record share subscriptions in the register, collect the agreed cash or property consideration, and issue the corresponding share certificates.
required_dossiers: First board resolution (minutes or unanimous written consent)
Share subscription ledger and issued share certificates
Statutory registers of directors, share transfers and by-laws
Bank resolution for corporate account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If share consideration is challenged by a creditor or the registrar, adopt a board rectification resolution with the sole shareholder's retroactive consent and amend the share register; any vacancy from a director's resignation is filled by written consent of the remaining directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Revenu Québec Registration (NEQ, GST/HST, QST and Payroll Accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec — clicSÉUR Affaires online service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the NEQ with Revenu Québec and simultaneously open the GST/HST and Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) accounts, noting that the small-supplier threshold of CAD 30,000 applies to GST/HST and Quebec aligns its QST registration threshold accordingly. Register for payroll source deductions if depot employees will be hired. Set fiscal reporting periods to match the cash flow of used-machinery remarketing.
required_dossiers: NEQ certificate issued at incorporation
Corporate bank account identification
Directors' identity documents (SIN or ITN) and residential addresses
Estimated supply volumes and planned payroll headcount
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is suspended for identity verification, provide notarized director attestations and certified identity copies through the clicSÉUR proof-of-identity queue; Revenu Québec reactivates the file within 10 business days with retroactive effect to the incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Site Occupancy Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipalité — Service de l'urbanisme et de l'inspection des bâtiments of the registered depot municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the permanent commercial occupation permit covering the storage yard, warehouse floor and equipment preparation bay. File a site plan showing excavator and roller storage positions, stormwater catch basins, property-line setbacks and the heavy-vehicle access route. Confirm the industrial zoning of the premises and obtain the municipal building completion certificate where a change of occupancy is required under the Construction Code.
required_dossiers: Lease or deed of the industrial premises
Site plan showing equipment storage and stormwater controls
Municipal application for a permanent commercial occupation permit
Zoning verification certificate or variance application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues a refusal or conditional permit, appeal to the municipal council review committee within 30 days or adjust the site plan to resolve parking, setback or stormwater objections, then resubmit the corrected dossier for reinstatement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RBQ Building, Electrical and Fire-Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) — Service de la sécurité dans les édifices, jointly with the municipal fire department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For warehouse mezzanines, heavy-equipment racks, crane anchoring and electrical installations, obtain the RBQ building certificate of approval and, where any alterations are performed, ensure the contracting firm holds an applicable RBQ contractor licence. Secure a fire-safety attestation from the municipal fire service covering aisle widths, extinguisher coverage and high-rack storage arrangements consistent with the Building Code (Q-2, r. 4.1).
required_dossiers: Engineer structural load certificates for racks and mezzanine systems
Electrical installation certificate from an RBQ-licensed master electrician
Municipal fire inspection record and suppression-equipment list
RBQ contractor licence evidence for any construction or alteration works
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If clearance is refused pending corrections, obtain the RBQ non-conformity list, contract a licensed engineer to verify corrective works, and pay the re-inspection fee; the usage authorization is issued upon filing the verified works with the Régie.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CNESST Registration and Environmental Storage Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) together with the Ministère de l'Environnement (MELCCFP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation as an employer with CNESST and maintain occupational-health files, WHMIS labeling for stored hydraulic oils and used engine coolant, and a hazardous-materials inventory covering waste oil, contaminated filters and drained hydraulic systems. If stored volumes of used oil or fuel exceed 2,000 litres, file a mandatory MELCCFP hazardous-materials storage declaration; for yards with stormwater outfalls, obtain the required wastewater discharge authorization.
required_dossiers: CNESST employer registration file
Hazardous-materials inventory and manifest records (used oil, glycol, contaminated filters)
WHMIS training completion log for depot personnel
MELCCFP storage declaration and, where applicable, a professional decontamination certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CNESST issues a notice of deficiency, submit a corrective investment plan with engineer-verified inputs within the 30-day compliance window; for MELCCFP matters, redesign storage below trigger thresholds or obtain covered-container permits and refile the attestation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) — Direction de l'industrie et du commerce; building-safety jurisdiction over the depot premises rests with the Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral wholesale trading permit is required for the remarketing of used construction excavators under Quebec law; the operative operating licenses are the municipal commercial occupation permit (permis d'affaires), the RBQ building certificate of approval, and the CNESST employer clearance for the warehouse and preparation yard.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction de l'évaluation environnementale des projets industriels
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: registration/exemption — a low-impact warehouse and resale operation for used machinery does not trigger a full Environmental Impact Assessment under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment; a declaration and compliance attestation are due only where on-site storage of hydrocarbon or hydraulic fluids exceeds the prescribed regulatory threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with the Regulation respecting the discharge into water bodies and municipal sewer by-laws (BOD/SS limits); VOC and particulate emissions from degreasing and equipment preparation must meet the Clean Air Regulation (Q-2, r. 4.1); used oil, glycol and hydraulic-fluid waste must be handled under the Hazardous Materials Regulation (Q-2, r. 32.2), including manifests, storage limits and the Quebec hazardous-waste tracking system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification under the Security Code (Q-2, r. 12.2) issued by the local fire department; RBQ structural-load certificates for racks, mezzanine and crane anchoring under the Building Code (Q-2, r. 4.1); CNESST workplace clearance including WHMIS 2015 labeling, emergency response procedures and machine-specific guarding under the Regulation respecting occupational health and safety; electrical permit from the RBQ and municipal inspection for any preparatory-works alterations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada for federal income tax, Business Number (BN), and GST/HST, with portal 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html) and Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-registration-online.html). Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) and Quebec corporation tax, with portal 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' (https://www.revenuquebec.ca). Quebec administers GST/HST within Quebec under a CRA service agreement; QST is a separate tax administered exclusively by Revenu Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Canadian statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) for a corporation is the 9-digit Business Number (BN) supplemented by program account codes (e.g., RT0001 for GST/HST, RC0001 for corporate income tax, and a Quebec QST program code issued by Revenu Québec). Step 1: determine whether the non-resident entity is 'carrying on business' in Canada/Quebec or is making taxable supplies in Canada. Step 2: register online via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) for the BN, corporate income tax account (RC), and GST/HST account (RT); non-residents without a Canadian address must file CRA Form RC391 (Application to Register a Non-Resident Business) and may designate a Canadian representative. Step 3: register for the QST with Revenu Québec simultaneously or subsequently (a separate QST registration application is required; non-residents appoint a representative on Revenu Québec Form LM-19-V). Step 4: registration is mandatory when quarterly-measured taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in Canada (GST/HST) or in Quebec (QST), or immediately for a non-resident carrying on business in Canada that does not qualify for the small-supplier exception (Excise Tax Act, subsection 240(1.1)). Step 5: retain the BN/QST registration confirmation, foreign articles of incorporation, and evidence of the Quebec permanent establishment for subsequent filing obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not employ a US-style 'check-the-box' election; a corporation is a separate taxpayer by operation of law. Relevant elections available to a used-machinery trading corporation include: (i) Income Tax Act (ITA) section 85 rollover election for tax-deferred transfer of capital property to a corporation; (ii) ITA section 22 election on the sale of accounts receivable; (iii) Excise Tax Act (ETA) section 156 election to deem supplies between closely related registrants to be for nil consideration (GST/HST neutrality); (iv) ETA section 227 Quick Method election for simplified GST/HST accounting, generally not attractive for exporters; (v) Quebec equivalents under the Quebec Sales Tax Act (section 1699) and the Taxation Act (section 85 parallel); and (vi) mandatory hybrid mismatch adjustment provisions under ITA sections 18.4-18.6, for which no elective carve-out exists. Treaty benefits are claimed on returns rather than by unilateral election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) under the Quebec Sales Tax Act. Quebec is a non-HST-participating province; GST at 5% and QST at 9.975% apply separately to taxable supplies made in Quebec, yielding a combined headline rate of 14.975%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (the small-supplier threshold under ETA section 148(1) for GST/HST and section 170 of the Quebec Sales Tax Act for QST; measured over the current calendar quarter plus the three preceding quarters, with non-residents counting only taxable supplies made in Canada or Quebec).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government API e-invoicing gateway, or digital stamping requirement for VAT/GST invoices. Standard paper, PDF, EDI, or PEPPOL e-invoices are accepted, and Canada is transitioning voluntarily to the Pan-Canadian PEPPOL/ Digital Interchange Canada standard. Exporters must retain invoices and export evidence in machine-readable format for six years under CRA record-keeping guidance (RC4047) and ETA section 286(1); Revenu Québec imposes parallel QST record-keeping obligations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A sale of used hydraulic excavators or rollers is zero-rated for GST/HST under ETA section 39(1) and Schedule VI, Part V, section 1, and for QST under section 59(1) of the Quebec Sales Tax Act, where the vendor ships or delivers the goods directly to a non-resident address outside Canada and obtains proof of export 'as part of the supply' (direct export). For indirect exports, where a non-resident purchaser takes delivery in Canada, zero-rating applies only if the goods are exported within 60 days of the sale and the vendor retains the export documentation (CRA GST/HST Memorandum 14-1). Ancillary services supplied to a non-resident in respect of the exported goods (e.g., offshore inspection or freight) may also be zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, sections 5-7 and QST equivalents. The exporting registrant may claim input tax credits attributable to the zero-rated export, generating net GST/QST refunds through ordinary returns.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: B13A Export Declaration (electronically filed via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) or licensed customs broker; mandatory for goods exceeding CAD 2,000 or for controlled and regulated goods under the Customs Act)
Original commercial invoice identifying seller, non-resident buyer, equipment make/model/serial number, HS codes (e.g., 8429.52, 8429.59), price, currency, and Incoterms
Through Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or highway truck manifest evidencing physical removal of the goods from Canada
CBSA export confirmation or customs broker clearance summary referencing the B13A declaration
Proof of payment: SWIFT MT103 wire confirmation, inward remittance certificate from the Canadian clearing bank, or export letter of credit settlement statement
Destination-country customs import entry or import declaration, where obtainable, to complete the export chain of evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec subject used-machinery export claims to heightened scrutiny for fictitious exports, circular transactions, documentary falsification, and goods returned to Canada. Civil penalties under the ETA include: subsection 285(1) net-tax deficiency penalty (5% of the understated amount plus 2% per month, capped at 20%); subsection 285.1(1) false statement penalty (25% of the tax that would have been evaded); and parallel QST penalties under the Quebec Sales Tax Act. Under ITA subsection 163(2), making a false statement on the corporate return carries a penalty of 50% of the income tax understated. Criminal liability may arise under ETA section 327 or ITA section 239 (fines of 50%-200% of evaded taxes and imprisonment up to 2 years), or under Quebec tax offences (fines up to 300% and imprisonment up to 5 years). Retrospective clawbacks follow the standard four-year reassessment window (ETA section 298(1), ITA subsection 152(4)), extended to ten years for gross negligence at the federal level and indefinitely for fraud, with compound daily interest at the prescribed rate. Directors are jointly and severally liable for unremitted GST/QST under ETA section 323 and the Quebec Sales Tax Act. Canada imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline under exchange control law; the 180-day settlement benchmark is adopted to mitigate CRA audit risk that export receivables outstanding beyond 180 days evidence non-arm's-length financing or uncollected proceeds subject to income tax recharacterization.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary and currency authority; foreign-exchange policy and administration rest with the Minister of Finance under the Currency Act and the Exchange Fund Act; prudential supervision of deposit-taking institutions is vested in the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/CFT and cross-border EFT reporting are administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); payments clearing infrastructure is operated by Payments Canada (Lynx, ACSS, Real-Time Rail).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free-floating, fully convertible Canadian dollar with no exchange-control regime on the current or capital account. Profit remittance by a Quebec business corporation is unrestricted, subject to Part XIII Income Tax Act withholding (25% statutory, reduced to 5-15% under tax treaties, e.g., Canada-US Convention) and to standard corporate filings (T1146/T1134). Inbound acquisitions or the establishment of a new non-cultural Canadian business trigger an Investment Canada Act post-closing notification within 37 days of implementation; review thresholds generally do not apply to a wholesale used-machinery trading entity. Section 261 of the Income Tax Act permits a USD functional-currency election, materially simplifying treasury accounting for USD-dominated heavy equipment trades.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio; export receipts in USD, EUR, or other currencies may be retained offshore or repatriated freely. For tax purposes, export revenue is recognized in the corporation's functional currency (default CAD), and a s. 261 election is available where USD is the predominant operating currency. Banks and PSPs must file electronic funds transfer reports with FINTRAC for cross-border wires of CAD 10,000 or more, requiring accurate remitter/beneficiary identification, invoice references, and a clear transaction purpose code on each MT103.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FX Hedge and Cross-Border Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability, with material legal constraints. Canada has no standalone electronic money institution licence; non-bank payment service providers (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer) must register under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) and cannot hold client escrow deposits, issue documentary letters of credit, or provide regulated bank-issued FX derivatives. Fintech rails are suitable only for operational sub-CAD 100,000 supplier disbursements and not for capital escrow, LC issuance, or treasury hedging, which must remain with a Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person KYC is the de facto industry standard: Schedule I banks require at least one director or appointed authorized signatory to appear physically at a Quebec branch (Montreal trade-finance centers are preferred) for a new corporate account where the majority of directors are non-residents. Wholly remote account opening for a newly incorporated, foreign-owned wholesale entity is not generally available. A Canadian-resident director, a Quebec-based authorized signatory, or a registered agent with banking powers of attorney should be appointed to satisfy enhanced customer due diligence, signature-card verification, and ongoing UBO monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk trade-based money-laundering classification applied to wholesale dealing in secondhand construction excavators and rollers, where machinery has no standardized fungible valuation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent equipment appraisals and auction valuations (e.g., Ritchie Bros. results), serial-number-tagged inventory ledger, executed purchase and sale contracts, original supplier invoices, bills of lading, pre-shipment inspection certificates, manufacturer ownership history, and customs declarations (ACI/AMS) to evidence genuine commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated Quebec Business Corporation with 100% non-resident beneficial owners and minimal local footprint, triggering shell-entity and nominee-director screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificat de constitution and Registraire des entreprises attestation, paid-up capital contribution records mirroring the bank-route wires, executed multi-year office lease in Quebec, in-province employee or independent sales-agent agreements, payroll records, and board resolutions authorizing the banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anticipated high-volume outbound disbursements to third-country auction houses, brokers, and freight forwarders that are not the invoice counterparties, creating payment-chain integrity concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved counterparty matrix with KYC/ownership confirmations, triangular trade-flow memorandum, three-way reconciliation ledgers matching purchase orders, auction settlement advices, logistics invoices, and bank-verified beneficial ownership declarations for each material payee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire transfers exceeding CAD 150,000 routed to jurisdictions flagged in FATF or Canadian sanctions screening, particularly for APAC origin used-equipment supply chains.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury hedging and payment-rationale memorandum, source-of-funds statements from the foreign parent and shareholders, export/import government filings, insurance certificates, broker escrow confirmations, and a sector-specific AML/CFT policy manual including transaction monitoring thresholds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity and shareholder-loan funding from non-residents must be wired via SWIFT MT103 into the designated CAD or USD operating account at National Bank of Canada or BMO, with the remitter legal name matching the corporate registry beneficial-ownership file, a precise remittance reference citing the subscription agreement or shareholder loan, and the contract date. Canadian banks will require a board resolution, signed subscription agreements, and FINTRAC EFT reporting for transfers of CAD 10,000 or more. Funding should be sequenced only after the Quebec entity is active in the Registraire des entreprises and the Investment Canada Act establishment notification window is understood, and all inbound flows must be entered in the corporate minute book to support the s. 261 functional-currency election and Part XIII withholding file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For used excavator procurement and resale settlements: (i) small auction deposits and supplier down payments are cleared by SWIFT MT103 wire transfer with contract-linked reference details; (ii) transactions above USD 100,000 are cleared through an irrevocable standby or commercial letter of credit issued by BMO or National Bank under SWIFT MT700, payable at sight or deferred 30-60 days, with beneficiary presentation of original bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and independent inspection certificate; (iii) interbank settlement of large-value CAD/USD payments runs through Lynx (the high-value clearing system) via the Canadian correspondent bank, with ACSS for domestic incidental payments. All rails must comply with FINTRAC EFT reporting and Canadian sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable FX forwards (tenor 1-12 months) executed under the bank's ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or short-form FX master
CAD/USD vanilla European options purchased from a Schedule I bank markets desk for downside protection on USD payables
Cross-currency swaps for long-term CAD-to-USD working-capital conversion where permanent USD liquidity is required

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on KRW and offshore CNY, permitted only where the underlying exposure arises from Korean or Chinese used-equipment/parts supply contracts, and executed under the bank's market-risk line
Embedded FX hedging through invoice-level spot rate fixing under SWIFT MT103 and MT700 trade documents, rather than speculative derivative positions

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: Name of annual return, corporate declaration, or franchise filing
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Financial penalties and timeline triggering administrative strike-off

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal Part I rate: 38% basic rate less 10% provincial abatement less 13% general rate reduction = 15%; provincial Quebec general rate: 11.5%; combined headline rate: 26.5%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction: federal 9% plus Quebec 3.2% on the first C$500,000 of active business income eligible for the SBD (combined 12.2%); entity controlled by non-residents is not a CCPC and pays 26.5%. No sector-specific incentive for used heavy-equipment wholesalers; standard deductions include cost of goods sold (purchase price, freight, import duties), capital cost allowance on depreciable assets, and arm's-length interest; foreign tax credits available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically via the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) EFILE/TELEFILE or certified third-party software; mandatory e-filing for most corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed no later than six months after the fiscal year-end (ITA s.150(1)). Federal balance of Part I tax payable: due two months after year-end, or three months for a CCPC that is eligible for the small business deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the full legal name exactly as incorporated under the CBCA or Quebec Business Corporations Act; trade names alone are insufficient.
A non-resident controlled Canadian corporation must obtain its own BN; a Canadian agent address may be provided for CRA correspondence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross wholesale revenue from sales of used excavators, rollers, and related parts, including deposits and progress payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all amounts in CAD using CRA prescribed exchange rates; include related-party sales and disclose them in Schedule 9 / TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of used machinery sold: acquisition price, freight, inspection, repair and refinishing costs, and import duties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer prices of imported used excavators from foreign related sellers must satisfy the arm's length standard; unsupported invoices are disregarded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after reserves, non-capital loss carryovers, and adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian-resident corporation, even if wholly foreign-owned, is taxable on worldwide income; no Part XIV branch election applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basic federal tax (38% less 10% abatement less 13% general rate reduction = 15%), minus credits such as foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The small business deduction (low 9% rate) is not available because the corporation is not controlled in Canada; apply general 15% federal rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (17% maximum); repeat failure within 3 years: 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months (50% maximum). Late payment interest: CRA prescribed rate compounded daily (approximately 7% annually in 2024) on unpaid balances.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return (Société), filed electronically through Revenu Quebec's Mon dossier d'entreprise or certified tax software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CO-17 must be filed no later than six months after the fiscal year-end (Quebec Tax Administration Act s.1000). Provincial balance due: two months after year-end generally, or three months for a CCPC eligible for the small business deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), legal name, and mailing address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors must provide a Quebec service address; a foreign mailing address is acceptable for correspondence but a Quebec agent should be designated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All income taxable in Quebec, including wholesale trading profit allocated to Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a corporation with foreign operations, allocate income under the Quebec allocation rules and the Canada-Quebec tax agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reduces the 11.5% Quebec rate to 3.2% on the first C$500,000 of eligible active business income for a qualified CCPC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable where non-residents control the corporation; enter zero and apply the 11.5% general rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Quebec income tax after statutory reductions, credits, and instalment payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No dividend withholding is integrated into CO-17; Part XIII withholding on dividends is handled separately through the CRA NR4 system.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Quebec penalties mirror federal: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of lateness (maximum 17%); repeat offender: 10% plus 2% per month (maximum 50%). Quebec interest accrues at the prescribed rate compounded daily on balances and overdue instalments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Federal Part XIII withholding tax of 25% on dividends (deemed or actual taxable dividends) paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident of Canada (ITA s.212(2)); no separate provincial dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a tax treaty reduced rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must (1) obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the treaty country's tax authority, (2) provide the Canadian paying corporation with a completed Form NR301/NR302 declaration of residency (or Form W-8BEN-E for US residents, with IRS Form 6166 on request), and (3) ensure the forms are available for CRA review. The withholding agent applies the treaty rate at source; representative treaty rates: US – 5% where the corporate shareholder owns 10% or more of voting shares, otherwise 15%; France – 5% for shareholdings of at least 10%, otherwise 15%. Excess tax is refunded through Form NR7-R if not applied at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory Part XIII rate 25%; reduced to 0% under most Canadian DTAs (US: 0% generally; France: 0% generally), subject to thin-capitalization and interest-stripping recharacterization as distributions under ITA s.18(4) and s.212(1). Royalties: statutory 25%; treaty rates: US – 10% (0% for certain literary/software copyrights), France – 10%; payments must be arm's length in amount.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Country-by-Country Report (Form RC4647): mandatory where the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue equals or exceeds C$750 million. Master File: mandatory for fiscal periods beginning on or after 1 April 2022 where group consolidated revenue equals or exceeds C$1 billion and the Canadian member has cross-border related-party revenues or expenses of at least C$100 million, or cross-border related-party financing balances of at least C$25 million. Local File / contemporaneous documentation under ITA s.247(4): required where any individual related-party transaction, or the aggregate cross-border related-party transactions, exceed C$1 million; documentation must exist before the filing deadline to constitute 'reasonable efforts' and avoid the 10% penalty.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) – preferred for standardized used excavators where comparable arm's length market prices exist
Resale Price Method – suited to wholesale remarketing where resale margins are verifiable
Cost Plus Method – appropriate for routine refurbishment and logistics services
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) – most commonly applied for distribution and trading functions
Profit Split Method – reserved for complex integrated operations with unique intangibles
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation regime; substance is nonetheless enforced through (a) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s.245; penalty of 25% of the disallowed tax benefit) and its Quebec counterpart (Quebec Tax Administration Act s.1075.7), (b) the corporate residence test based on central management and control (ITA s.250), (c) the BEPS Multilateral Instrument principal purpose test for treaty benefits, and (d) the requirement for a genuine Canadian establishment with board minutes, personnel, bank accounts, and transaction records in Quebec. A mail-drop office with no operative substance in Quebec will be disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating gross sales of used construction machinery, maintaining duplicate invoicing systems for cash or wire transactions, or inflating inventory cost invoices from related foreign suppliers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil: gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated federal tax (ITA s.163(2)) plus interest; the same penalty applies provincially under the Quebec Tax Administration Act. Criminal: ITA s.239(1) – fine of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to 2 years on summary conviction or up to 5 years on indictment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false returns or direct concealed sales face personal criminal liability for tax evasion; courts may impose travel bans and passport surrender where flight risk exists. The corporate veil may be pierced for fraud or abuse of the corporate personality under art. 317 of the Civil Code of Quebec, exposing directors to civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling used excavators to an offshore related marketing company below the arm's length margin, or paying excessive management fees to a foreign affiliate, with no contemporaneous transfer pricing study or Master File.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA re-determination to the arm's length amount plus a 10% penalty on the net transfer pricing adjustment (ITA s.247(3)) where the net adjustment exceeds the lesser of C$5,000,000 or 10% of gross revenue; interest applies from the taxation year. Quebec applies parallel adjustment powers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically assessed for transfer pricing penalties; however, deliberate orchestration of non-arm's length prices with intent to evade tax attracts criminal liability under s.239, personal fines, and civil delictual liability to the corporation.
